question: Which of the following gases get released when dilute sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) reacts with magnesium (Mg)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**H2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When dilute sulphuric acid (H2SO4) reacts with magnesium (Mg), hydrogen gas (H2) is released.
 
• The chemical equation for the reaction is: Mg + H2SO4 → MgSO4 + H2.
 
• Magnesium (Mg) is a highly reactive metal and reacts vigorously with dilute acids.
 
• The reaction of a metal with an acid typically produces a salt and hydrogen gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sulphuric Acid (H2SO4)**

 
 
• It is a strong mineral acid with various industrial applications.
 
• It is used in the production of fertilizers, in petroleum refining, and in wastewater processing.
 
• H2SO4 is highly corrosive and can cause severe burns.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas (H2)**
 
 
• Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe.
 
• It is commonly used in the chemical industry and in fuel cells for energy production.
 
• Hydrogen gas is colorless, odorless, and highly flammable.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)**
 
 
• Magnesium is a lightweight metal with a silvery-white appearance.
 
• It is used in the production of alloys, in the automotive industry, and in the manufacture of fireworks and flares.
 
• Magnesium is essential for all living cells and is the 11th most abundant element by mass in the human body.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactions of Metals with Acids**
 
 
• Metals react with acids to produce a salt and hydrogen gas.
 
• The general reaction can be represented as: Metal + Acid → Salt + Hydrogen gas.
 
• The reactivity of the metal determines the vigor of the reaction.
